claude.sample_unit: participants (42,937 CKB general population; 14,125 JBPCD type 2 diabetes)

links.outcome: Calibration (E/O ratio, Brier score) and discrimination of original versus locally recalibrated CVD risk models
links.effect: Recalibration markedly improved calibration and reduced Brier scores with little change in discrimination; original E/O 1.47-3.78 in general cohort and 0.32-2.70 in T2D cohort.
links.quote: Recalibration markedly improved calibration and reduced Brier scores, with little change in discrimination.

links.outcome: Performance of existing risk models on local Chinese cohort data versus reference outcomes
links.effect: Original models were poorly calibrated, with systematic overprediction in the general population cohort (E/O 1.47-3.78) and heterogeneous miscalibration in the type 2 diabetes cohort (E/O 0.32-2.70).
links.quote: Original models were poorly calibrated, with systematic overprediction in the general population cohort (E/O 1.47-3.78) and heterogeneous miscalibration in the type 2 diabetes cohort (E/O 0.32-2.70).

links.outcome: Discrimination of risk models in general population versus type 2 diabetes population
links.effect: Discrimination was higher in the general population cohort than in the type 2 diabetes cohort (C-statistic 0.723-0.778 vs. 0.584-0.629).
